messages:
maria: SLO burn alert just fired for hosted inference ingress — 5xx rate jumped to 2.3% in us-west-2 over the last 10m. Dashboard: https://grafana.internal/redwood/prod/ingress-5xx (check the red spikes). Can folks triage?

sre-bot: [ALERT] prod.ingress.5xx_rate > 2% for 10m — triggered at 2026-03-15T09:05:21Z :warning:

leah: support ticket INC-46291 from Acme Apps reporting timeouts + 502s for generation endpoints. They say failures started ~09:00 and are seeing lots of client retries/billing hits. They sent example request IDs: rQ-7a2f, rQ-7a31.

oliver: I’m looking at traces — sampling seems fine for some services but there’s a trace gap between gateway -> serving runtime for many of the failed requests. Span `serve.generate.forward` missing. Probably times out at gateway before runtime reports.

jason: Any recent deploys to serving runtime or gateway?

deploy-bot: Deployment record: service=serving-runtime, version=v2026-03-15-kernel-batch, started rollout 2026-03-15T08:30Z, 60% complete.

jason: That rollout touched the new batching kernel and kernel selection heuristic. Rolling back or pausing could be worthwhile. I can pause the rollout.

maria: Before rollback, can we confirm node-level metrics? I see a subset of GPU hosts with high accept queue length and tail latencies. Query I'm running:

```
# Loki query (approx)
{job="serving-runtime"} | json | status="500" | unwrap latency_ms | histogram_over_time(5m, 50ms)
```

Those nodes show p95 > 2s.

oliver: Also seeing increased connection resets at the ingress proxy to those hosts — possible kernel change introduced longer per-request scheduling stalls, causing gateway timeouts.

leah: Acme provided a curl repro we can ask them to run (if we change timeouts first):

```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"large-gen","prompt":"hello"}' \
  https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate
```

If they run that repeatedly it reproduces 502s for them.

jason: Mitigation plan suggestion: 1) pause rollout to new kernel, 2) route traffic away from problematic hosts (remove from LB), 3) bump gateway upstream timeout from 30s -> 45s temporary, 4) enable fallback routing to quantized smaller model variant for the hosted pool to reduce runtime latency. I can pause the rollout now.

maria: Please pause rollout and remove hosts with accept-queue > 50 from the pool. I'll also create a temporary alert to notify if p95 > 1.5s for next 1h so we can catch reappearance.

deploy-bot: Rollout paused: serving-runtime v2026-03-15-kernel-batch (paused at 60% by jason).

jason: Removing 3 hosts from lb: host-rt-12, host-rt-17, host-rt-21. Command used: `infractl lb detach --pool serving-prod --hosts host-rt-12,host-rt-17,host-rt-21`

oliver: After detaching we see 5xx rate dropping toward baseline. Grafana shows drop from 2.3% -> 0.6% over ~8m. Tracing gap reduced as well.

leah: Let me update Acme: we paused a rollout affecting the serving runtime and routed traffic away from affected hosts. Ask them to re-run the curl and send request IDs if they still see failures.

maria: Temporary gateway config to increase timeout (applied):

```
# nginx-like gateway snippet (applied to gateway-config/prod)
proxy_read_timeout 45s;
proxy_connect_timeout 10s;
proxy_send_timeout 45s;
```

Note: this is a short-lived mitigation, not a long-term fix.

oliver: Follow-ups for post-incident: 1) revert kernel selection heuristic change or add canary guard rails (only route to hosts with warm KV caches), 2) add more granular tracing so gateway->runtime forwarding spans always emit before timeout, 3) tighten pre-deploy perf checks (p95 under synthetic workloads).

jason: I'll file a bug and assign to eng-runtime (BUG-1184). Also will coordinate a rollback plan to fully revert if we don't have a safe kernel revision by EOD.

maria: Support/action items: 
- leah: confirm Acme repro after mitigation and capture any remaining request IDs
- jason: follow up rollback if we see recurrence
- oliver: add temporary alert and capture full log bundle for the three hosts
- maria: write an incident page and schedule postmortem

leah: Confirmed with Acme — they re-tested and failures dropped significantly. They still saw one 502 (rQ-7a31) which we have logs for. They're okay for now but want a timeline. I'll send their contact an ETA.

maria: Thanks all. We'll keep this thread open as we complete the postmortem and any config changes. Tagging for follow-up: @eng-runtime, @observability. :white_check_mark:
